notes: EBIT mapping: historical and forecast EBIT use the 10-K line item “Earnings before interest and taxes” (EBIT). ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Campbells-Annual-Report-Bookmarked.pdf))

D&A mapping: historical D&A uses “Depreciation and amortization” from the consolidated cash flow statement (total). ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Campbells-Annual-Report-Bookmarked.pdf))

Capex mapping: historical capex uses “Purchases of plant assets” (capital expenditures total). ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Campbells-Annual-Report-Bookmarked.pdf))

NWC construction (used for historical values and as the basis for NWC % of sales assumptions): (Total current assets − Cash and cash equivalents) − (Total current liabilities − Short-term borrowings). Campbell reports negative working capital; model keeps it slightly negative in forecasts. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/2024-Annual-Report.pdf))

NOL utilization: the FY2025 annual report provides the aggregate tax loss carryforward balance but does not provide a directly usable NOL utilization percent for modeling; therefore nol_utilization_pct is set to null. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Campbells-Annual-Report-Bookmarked.pdf))

Comps fields: Finviz provides EV/Sales, EV/EBITDA, and forward P/E; strict EV/NTM Revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA could not be confirmed as “NTM” in the retrieved pages, so EV/Sales is used as a proxy and EV/EBITDA is treated as the available enterprise multiple metric. ([finviz.com](https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=GIS))

Fiscal-year alignment: FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 are the last three completed fiscal years as of 2026-03-21 (fiscal years ended July 30, 2023; July 28, 2024; Aug 3, 2025). ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Campbells-Annual-Report-Bookmarked.pdf))

catalysts: Evidence of demand stabilization and improved gross profit dynamics as tariff and input-cost impacts normalize or are mitigated. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/newsroom/press-releases/campbells-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results/))

Operational delivery of cost savings and route-to-market execution (margin durability and operating leverage). ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/2024-Annual-Report.pdf))

Continued capital returns (dividends and buybacks) consistent with cash flow generation and leverage management. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/newsroom/press-releases/campbells-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results/))
company_overview: The Campbell’s Company is a North America-focused branded food company with Meals & Beverages and Snacks operating segments. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/2024-Annual-Report.pdf))

FY2025 reported net sales of $10.253 billion and EBIT (earnings before interest and taxes) of $1.124 billion, reflecting substantial non-cash and restructuring/other line items. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Campbells-Annual-Report-Bookmarked.pdf))

Capital allocation emphasizes returning cash to shareholders (dividends and buybacks) while funding ongoing manufacturing/network and compliance-related capital expenditures. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Campbells-Annual-Report-Bookmarked.pdf))
current_context: In fiscal Q2 2026 (ended Feb 1, 2026), EBIT decreased to $273 million from $327 million, driven primarily by lower adjusted gross profit and related cost impacts. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/newsroom/press-releases/campbells-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results/))

Management lowered FY2026 guidance: organic net sales to (2)% to (1)% and adjusted EBIT to (20)% to (17)% (excluding the impact of the 53rd week and certain divestiture effects). ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/newsroom/press-releases/campbells-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results/))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes a modest contraction in FY2026 followed by gradual stabilization as cost savings and trade/product execution offset some volume headwinds. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/newsroom/press-releases/campbells-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results/))

Forecast EBIT margins move from ~10.5% in FY2026 back toward low-11% steady-state by FY2030 (reflecting normalized operating performance versus FY2025 levels). ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Campbells-Annual-Report-Bookmarked.pdf))

D&A scales with revenue at ~4.25% of sales and capex remains ~4–4.5% of sales, consistent with recent historical cash flow patterns. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Campbells-Annual-Report-Bookmarked.pdf))

Negative working capital remains a structural feature in the model (supplier/trade funding), with NWC staying slightly negative as a % of sales. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/2024-Annual-Report.pdf))
key_risks: Tariffs, commodity inflation, and unfavorable supply-chain impacts could pressure margins more than assumed in the base case. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/newsroom/press-releases/campbells-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results/))

Consumer trade-down, competitive promotional intensity, or volume/mix pressure could slow revenue growth and delay margin recovery. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/newsroom/press-releases/campbells-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results/))

Working capital could deteriorate (less negative NWC) if trade terms or inventory/payables dynamics change. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/2024-Annual-Report.pdf))

valuation_summary: DCF uses WACC of ~8.2%, terminal growth of 2.0%, and a Gordon-growth terminal value to reflect a mature packaged-food profile. ([thecampbellscompany.com](https://www.thecampbellscompany.com/newsroom/press-releases/campbells-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results/))

Peer triangulation uses EV/EBITDA and forward P/E from Finviz; EV/Sales is used as a practical proxy for EV/NTM Revenue because strict NTM revenue multiples were not reliably available in the retrieved dataset. ([finviz.com](https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=GIS))
